findings.claim: The guard `#if !NETSTANDARD2_0 && !NETFRAMEWORK` drops the attribute from all generated code when the consuming project targets netstandard2.0 or .NET Framework, yet `System.Diagnostics.CodeAnalysis.ExcludeFromCodeCoverageAttribute` exists on both. It ships in netstandard 2.0 and in System.dll since .NET Framework 4.0, and it is valid on classes. The condition is broader than the derived criterion needs: that criterion asks for conditional emission only where the attribute does not exist. As a result, netstandard2.0 libraries (a very common MessagePack consumer TFM) and .NET Framework projects still get no coverage exclusion. That breaks 'All generated code is decorated with ExcludeFromCodeCoverage'. The same guard appears in every template: Formatter, StringKeyFormatter, Enum, Union, Resolver and CompositeResolver.

receipt_plan.detail: Run Receipts.GeneratedTests.ExcludeFromCodeCoverageNetStandardTests.GeneratedTypesHaveAttributeWhenNetStandard20Defined. It runs MessagePackGenerator with preprocessor symbol NETSTANDARD2_0 and asserts every generated class symbol carries ExcludeFromCodeCoverageAttribute. On head the #if strips the attribute, so the test fails.
